title: 3D Molecular Structure Viewer (Ball-and-Stick Model)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a 3D molecular structure viewer (Ball-and-Stick model) for educational demonstrations.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
// Write your code here
</script>

[Molecule Presets]
(1) A dropdown with id="moleculeSelect" switches among three molecules: Water (H2O), Ethanol (C2H5OH), and Caffeine (C8H10N4O2). The option values or displayed names must exactly match the following strings for testing: "Water", "Ethanol", and "Caffeine".

[Atoms and Bonds]
(2) Atoms are spheres with the following colors and radii: C dark gray, radius=0.3; H white, radius=0.15; O red, radius=0.28; N blue, radius=0.26.
(3) Chemical bonds use cylinders (CylinderGeometry) to connect the centers of two atoms. Represent a single bond with one cylinder; represent a double bond with two parallel cylinders that are slightly offset.
(4) Hard-code the 3D coordinates of each atom in the code (approximately realistic geometry; the scale may be uniformly adjusted):
  - Water: O at (0,0,0); H at (0.76, 0.59, 0) and (-0.76, 0.59, 0), with a bond angle of approximately 104.5°.
  - Ethanol: 9 atoms in total (the C–C–O backbone and hydrogens), with coordinates arranged as a reasonable 3D geometry.
  - Caffeine: 24 atoms in total, with coordinates based on standard ball-and-stick model topology (fused rings + substituents).

[Interaction and Camera]
(5) Use OrbitControls and enable auto-rotate (the molecule automatically rotates slowly).
(6) When an atom is clicked, highlight that atom (for example, using emissive or scale), and display its element symbol, English name, and atomic number in the DOM element with id="atomInfo".
(7) A display mode button with id="displayMode" cycles or switches among three modes:
  - "ball-and-stick": ball-and-stick (the radii specified above are used and the bonds are visible)
  - "space-filling": space-filling (the spheres are significantly enlarged and the bonds are hidden)
  - "wireframe": display only the bonds (or bond wireframes); atoms may be hidden or shown as extremely small spheres
  window.__3D_STATE__.displayMode must be one of the hyphenated English strings above.

[HUD]
(8) id="atomCount": the number of atoms in the current molecule; id="bondCount": the number of bonds; id="currentMolecule": the current molecule name ("Water" / "Ethanol" / "Caffeine").

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame. It must include at least:
- atomCount, bondCount: integers
- currentMolecule: string
- displayMode: "ball-and-stick" | "space-filling" | "wireframe"
- atoms: array, with each item in the form { element, x, y, z, radius }, where element is "H"|"C"|"N"|"O", etc.
- selectedAtom: when selected, an object in the form { element, symbol, name, atomicNumber, x, y, z }; when no atom is selected, null

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
